query: Review landing.html and tell me what's wrong with it. Be specific about locations.
expected_behavior: Findings are reported as landing.html:<line> locations, grouped under the file, with no preamble essay

Names the generated-look tells concretely: the indigo/violet gradient background, the stacked triple box-shadow, one border-radius reused on every element, the tracked ALL-CAPS eyebrow, the 'A · B · C' middot meta string, the '→' appended to the button label, the italic single-word accent in the headline, and the em dash in visible copy
Flags the removed focus ring (`outline: none` on .cta:focus and .icon-btn:focus) and prescribes `:focus-visible` with a visible indicator rather than `:focus`
Flags that the entrance animation and the hover transform have no `prefers-reduced-motion` reduced variant
Flags `transition: all` and requires listing `transform, opacity` (compositor-only) explicitly
Flags the `` with no width/height as a CLS risk, the icon-only `
Flags `maximum-scale=1, user-scalable=no` as a zoom-blocking anti-pattern

Flags 'Loading...' (should be 'Loading…'), the hardcoded 03/04/2026 date (should use `Intl.DateTimeFormat`), and the placeholder content tells ('Acme', 'John Doe', 99.99%/50%/1234567 fake-perfect numbers, 'Elevate'/'seamlessly' filler verbs)
Gives a concrete replacement for each finding rather than only naming the problem

query: I need a landing page for a small independent bike-frame builder who hand-brazes steel touring frames in Bristol. Before you write any code, give me the visual direction.
expected_behavior: States a one-line design read (page kind, audience, visual language) before proposing anything
Proposes a design plan with 4-6 named colors given as hex values, not vague color words
Names the typefaces and the role of each (display vs body), and does not default to Inter
Includes at least one ASCII wireframe of the page structure with alignment stated

Explicitly checks the plan against the generated-design clusters it must avoid (cream+serif+terracotta, near-black+acid accent, purple/indigo gradient, uniform rounded card grid, ALL-CAPS eyebrows) and says what was changed after that check
Grounds the choices in the subject matter (steel, brazing, touring, Bristol) rather than generic SaaS language
Withholds implementation code until the direction is agreed, or clearly separates the plan from any code

query: Our design system wants one number for minimum interactive target size on the web. What does WCAG actually require at AA, and where does 44x44 come from?
expected_behavior: States that WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is Level AA and requires at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels
Attributes 44 by 44 CSS pixels to WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), which is Level AAA, and/or to Apple HIG's 44pt and Material's 48dp platform guidance rather than to WCAG AA
Mentions the SC 2.5.8 exceptions (spacing via a 24 CSS px diameter circle test, equivalent control, inline targets, user-agent default, essential)
Does not present 44x44 as the WCAG AA minimum

query: Read slow_orders_query.sql. It takes about 14 seconds on PostgreSQL 16. Explain from the SQL text alone why it is slow and what to change. Do not install, start or query any database, and do not write any files - answer in chat only.
expected_behavior: Does not read the frontend-design skill (skill_read is false); nothing about typography, color tokens, WCAG or Core Web Vitals appears

Answers as a SQL/database question: the LOWER(c.email) LIKE predicate defeating the index, the NOT IN subquery, the LEFT JOIN made inner by the WHERE clause on o.placed_at, and the item-level fan-out inflating SUM
Recommends EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) and concrete index or rewrite options

query: Review sections.html as a design pass, not a code-quality pass. It is a nine-section marketing page. Tell me which parts read as machine-generated and give me the specific fix for each, with locations.
expected_behavior: Counts the small uppercase/tracking eyebrows mechanically and states that the page exceeds the budget: nine sections carry nine such labels, against a ceiling of roughly one per three sections

Rejects the enumerated eyebrows themselves ('001 · QUIETLY IN USE AT', '002 · THE HARDWARE' through '009 · HOW IT WORKS') as section-numbering labels, and prescribes dropping them rather than renaming them
Flags the run of three consecutive image-and-text split sections (spinning, brazing, tempering) as exceeding the alternation cap, and names a different layout family to break the run

Flags the col-span-7 headline plus col-span-5 floating explainer as the split-header pattern, and the 'Each of these is a process we run today, not a roadmap promise' line as a micro-meta sentence to delete

Flags the six-cell grid holding five items (the trailing empty white card) and requires the grid be reshaped to the content count rather than padded, and notes the all-white-on-white cells need real visual variation
Flags the bg-amber-50 quote section sitting inside an otherwise zinc-950 page as a mid-page theme inversion
Flags the div-built order-desk panel in the hero as a fake product screenshot, including its fake version footer ('v0.6.2-rc.1 · last sync 4s ago · main')

Flags the hero stack as overloaded: the 'INVITE-ONLY PREVIEW' version label, the 'Marrow · No. 01 · The 6-quart' sub-eyebrow, the subtext far past roughly 20 words, the pt-40 top padding, and the trust strip under the CTAs
Flags the decoration strip 'STEEL. FIRE. PATIENCE.', the '↓ Scroll to explore' cue, the 'LIS 14:23 · 18°C' locale strip, and the footer 'Build 0048 · v1.4.2' version stamp
Flags the wrapping seven-item navigation and its py-10 height, and the decorative status dot repeated before every nav link
Flags the logo wall printing a category label under each wordmark, and that the wordmarks are plain text rather than real marks

Flags the ten-row specification table carrying both border-t and border-b on every row and proposes a different component (grouped clusters, spec cards, or featured-plus-disclosure) rather than a tidier table
Flags the filled-track comparison bars, the 'Stage 1 / Stage 2 / Stage 3' generic step labels, and the duplicate-intent CTAs ('Get in touch' and "Let's talk")
Flags the quote running well past three lines and its name-only attribution, and the invented precise numbers (92% fill, 4.1x pass, 5.8 mm, 13.4 lb) presented as specifications

query: Our checkout page gets complaints that it is slow. Lighthouse gives it a performance score of 98 on my laptop. I also added `onLCP(v => console.log(v))` from the web-vitals package and the numbers look fine in my browser, so I have field data too. CrUX has no record for the URL. I cannot run the page locally, I only have the source. Tell me what I actually know and what I should do next.
expected_behavior: States that the in-browser `onLCP(console.log)` reading is a single-session lab observation, not field data, and that it becomes field data only when values are reported to a collector and aggregated across real sessions
States that a Lighthouse category score is not the evidence: cites metric values instead, and notes the score's weighting and audit set change between versions
Treats the missing CrUX record as unavailable rather than passing, and does not conclude the page is fine
Resolves the good-lab / complaints split by looking for the failing segment (device, route, cache state, connection) rather than accepting the passing local run as a defence
States that findings read from source alone are hypotheses, names the measurement that would confirm each, and does not assert that LCP, INP or CLS is failing
Recommends per-route p75 reporting rather than a site-wide average when field collection is set up

query: Clicking a filter chip on our product grid feels frozen for about half a second. INP measures 550ms. My onClick handler is one line, it just sets a state flag, and I profiled the handler itself at under 2ms. Why is INP still bad and what do I change?
expected_behavior: Splits INP into input delay, processing time and presentation delay, and states that the dominant phase must be identified from a trace before changing the handler
Explains that a 2ms handler behind an already-busy main thread is an input-delay problem, so rewriting the handler cannot move the metric
Identifies presentation delay (style, layout, paint of the re-rendered grid before the next frame) as the other candidate, distinct from the handler's own cost
Recommends painting the visible feedback first and yielding between chunks of the expensive work rather than doing it all in one task
Does not answer only with generic advice to debounce the handler or to virtualize the list

query: Here is our company site: a 2016-era Bootstrap 3 marketing site, about 20 pages, decent search traffic. It looks dated. Modernize it.
expected_behavior: Classifies the job before proposing visuals: preserve the existing brand versus start visually from scratch, and asks once if the brief does not settle it

Requires an audit before any change: existing brand tokens (color, type, radii, logo treatment), information architecture and conversion paths, which content blocks are doing work, and a dial reading of the current site as the starting point rather than the baseline
Names what must not change silently: URL and slug structure, primary navigation labels, form field names and order, the logo, and legal or consent copy
Orders the work by visual lift per unit of risk, typography and spacing before recomposition, and stops when the brief is satisfied instead of proposing a full rebuild by default
States that existing accessibility behaviour (focus states, alt text, keyboard paths, contrast) must not regress
Does not open with a list of visual treatments to apply (new font, gradients, animations) as the first action

query: I am building the settings surface for a Shopify app that merchants open inside the Shopify admin. Give me the visual direction and the component approach.
expected_behavior: Names Polaris as the required foundation for Shopify admin surfaces rather than proposing a hand-built or generic component set
States the honesty rule: install and use the official package instead of recreating its CSS, and do not import its tokens only to override most of them
States that one design system governs the project, and does not mix a second component system into the same tree
Recognizes that an embedded admin surface constrains the visual direction: the host application's conventions win over a distinctive marketing aesthetic
Does not produce a landing-page style design plan (hero, accent palette, display typeface) for an embedded admin form
